record.original_question: Explain the paradox that generic steady three-dimensional Euler fields appear topologically regular while Beltrami fields can realize arbitrarily complicated topology, and determine the natural notion of genericity for steady fields.

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Explain this paradox: what is a typical steady field and what genericity notion is natural for steady fields? It is worth mentioning that the notion of a typical object in fluid dynamics might be quite different from the standard one. For instance, as discussed in Section 6.1 stream functions of steady 2D flows always have analytical levels even if they have only finite smoothness across the levels. In [111] the authors considered slightly compressible 3D vector fields and their incompressible limit to explain the above paradox. The paper [42] also sheds more light on this problem: the levels of the Bernoulli function cannot be spheres. It turned out that the topology of Beltrami fields can be arbitrarily complicated. In [40] it was established that for any finite link L ⊂ R3 and any nonzero real number λ one can deform the link L by a C ∞ diffeomorphism of R3 , arbitrarily close to the identity in any C m norm, such that the image of the link becomes a set of vortex lines of a Beltrami field v with the eigenvalue λ 25

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider stationary solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on R^3 (or a Riemannian 3-manifold), i.e., divergence-free vector fields v satisfying (v · ∇)v = −∇p for some pressure function p. Two classes of such fields are of particular interest:

(i) Fields v whose Bernoulli function b = p + |v|^2/2 is nonconstant; by Arnold's structure theorem, away from critical points of b the trajectories of v lie on the level sets {b = const}, which are unions of tori and cylinders, giving such fields a "topologically tame" structure.

(ii) Beltrami fields, i.e., divergence-free vector fields satisfying curl v = λ v for some nonzero constant λ; these have constant Bernoulli function and can exhibit arbitrarily complicated topology. In particular, given any finite link L ⊂ R^3 and any nonzero λ ∈ R, there exists a C^∞ diffeomorphism of R^3 arbitrarily close to the identity in any C^m norm whose image of L is a set of vortex lines of some Beltrami field with eigenvalue λ.

This produces an apparent paradox: a "generic" steady Euler field looks like type (i) and is topologically simple, yet the subclass of Beltrami fields (type (ii)) realizes arbitrarily complicated topology of vortex lines.

Problem. Provide a mathematical explanation of this paradox by formulating an appropriate, natural notion of genericity for steady three-dimensional Euler fields under which:
(a) a typical steady Euler field is topologically tame (its trajectories lie on a regular family of two-dimensional level surfaces of the Bernoulli function), and
(b) the rich topological complexity exhibited by Beltrami fields is consistently accounted for within this notion of typicality.

Specify the function space, topology, and measure-theoretic or Baire-category sense in which "generic" is to be understood, and prove that the proposed notion yields these two properties.
artifact.category_tag: steady Euler flows and Beltrami fields
artifact.status_search_result: The question of a natural notion of genericity for steady 3D Euler fields reconciling Arnold's structure theorem with the topological flexibility of Beltrami fields appears to remain open. Partial progress exists: slightly compressible perturbations have been used to interpret the paradox, results on Bernoulli level sets (e.g., they cannot be spheres) have been obtained, and isolated/stable steady solutions and almost-global generalized Beltrami fields have been studied, but no widely accepted definitive notion of "typical steady Euler field" has been established.

status_evidence.title: Steady Euler flows and Beltrami fields in high dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how Beltrami fields relate to steady Euler flows, with paradoxical behavior in higher dimensions where Beltrami fields need not be Euler flows.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between Beltrami fields and typical steady Euler flows continues to be actively investigated, indicating the genericity question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Knots and links in steady solutions of the Euler equation
status_evidence.snippet: For any finite link L and nonzero λ, one can deform L by a small diffeomorphism to obtain vortex lines of a Beltrami field with eigenvalue λ.
status_evidence.claim: Beltrami fields realize arbitrarily complicated topology, establishing one side of the paradox.

status_evidence.title: Isolated steady solutions of the 3D Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on isolation and rigidity of steady 3D Euler solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research continues to probe the structure space of steady Euler fields without a settled genericity framework.
